A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same performative-prediction work. Their main text, equations, five figures, and appendices support comparison, including the ride-share study relocated to Appendix J in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original credit-scoring and ride-share simulations, plus a numerical illustration of the theoretical lower bound.

after.justification: V2 retains these original simulation results, including the experimental results in Appendices I and J.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a proximal ARM update with a penalty on movement from the previous iterate (Equation 18), generalized with an additional quadratic regularizer in Appendix F.1. The original distribution-averaging method and experimental implementations are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use Give Me Some Credit with Resample-if-Rejected, the Boston Uber/Lyft pricing game, and the synthetic lower-bound illustration. Moving the ride-share study from Section 7.2 to Appendix J does not change coverage.

E2.justification: The application comparisons retain aggregation windows 1, 2, 4, t/2, and all; Figure 2 retains windows 1 through 5. The newly discussed proximal variants are not experimentally evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: The metrics and retained experimental settings are unchanged: credit scoring uses delta 0.55, 50 iterations, and Adam with learning rate 3e-4; ride-share uses 25 demand samples, 40 retraining steps, and regularization 70. V2 reports no revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The aggregation-window comparisons, lower-bound illustration, and credit-scoring and ride-share case studies are retained. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 500 credit-scoring runs and 200 ride-share runs. The credit-scoring initialization and shared-within-run sampling descriptions are unchanged, with no new uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The matched experimental plots retain their numerical trajectories, rankings, and reported convergence trends. V1 Figures 4 and 5 become v2 Figures 5 and 4, respectively; the new transient-risk qualification discusses an existing plot.

T1.justification: Theorem 4 changes the reported convergence threshold for sqrt(epsilon) M/gamma from approximately 1.035 to 1.155, supported by a substantially rewritten n-snapshot derivation in Appendix E. V2 also adds proximal ARM lower bounds, proximal RRM convergence and fixed-point proofs, and revised auxiliary lemmas. Assumption 5 corrects the Lipschitz condition from the gradient in z to the gradient in theta.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims of improved RRM guarantees, tight lower bounds, historical-data ARM, and empirical convergence benefits. Revised novelty wording does not substantially redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix L distinguishes broader stability conditions from necessarily faster convergence and states limitations concerning stochastic settings and gradient-method extensions. Appendix I newly acknowledges that larger windows can incur worse intermediate performative risk despite smoother trajectories.

D1.justification: V2 discloses A100-40G GPUs and runs taking a few minutes for credit scoring, and CPU execution taking a few seconds for ride-share. It removes v1's explicit code-repository link; this changes access information without establishing that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Drusvyatskiy and Xiao, Hardt and colleagues, Li and Wai, Nesterov, and Schauder. It connects proximal ARM to earlier proximal RRM and identifies Nesterov's lower-bound construction as inspiration, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted abstract and introduction rewrites, standardizes ARM terminology, adds descriptive theorem titles and a main-text proof sketch, and moves the ride-share subsection to Appendix J. Much of the existing prose and main section order remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main text with a single-column layout and changes typography, headers, and figure sizing and placement. Figure 1 leaves the title page, Figures 2 and 3 appear together, and the ride-share figure moves to Appendix J.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful proximal analysis, clearer limitations, and hardware details, but its stronger convergence guarantee has unresolved support. Appendix E bounds an n-step squared displacement using n m_t^2 although the stated maximum only guarantees n^2 m_t^2; v1 contains a related two-step gap. This prevents confidently crediting the central tightening as an improvement, while removal of the code link also offsets better implementation disclosure.
